question:
The vertices of a triangle are $A(2,3)$, $B(-1,1)$, and $C(4,k)$.

(a) Form the determinant representing twice the area of $\triangle ABC$.

(b) Determine the values of $k$ if the area of the triangle is $8$ square units.

(c) Find the area of the triangle when $k=7$.
explanation:
(a)
The area of a triangle with vertices $(x_1,y_1)$, $(x_2,y_2)$, and $(x_3,y_3)$ is
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}x_1 & y_1 & 1\\x_2 & y_2 & 1\\x_3 & y_3 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
Therefore,
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 1\\-1 & 1 & 1\\4 & k & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$

(b)
Expanding the determinant,
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|2(1-k)-3(-1-4)+(-k-4)|$$
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|2-2k+15-k-4|$$
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|13-3k|$$
Given that the area is $8$ square units,
$$\frac{1}{2}|13-3k|=8$$
$$|13-3k|=16$$
Thus,
$$13-3k=16\quad\text{or}\quad13-3k=-16$$
Hence,
$$k=-1\quad\text{or}\quad k=\frac{29}{3}$$

(c)
When $k=7$,
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|13-21|=\frac{1}{2}(8)=4$$
Therefore, the area is $4$ square units.

options.A:
(a) Twice the area is $\left|\begin{vmatrix}2&3&1\\-1&1&1\\4&k&1\end{vmatrix}\right|=|13-3k|$
(b) $k=1$ or $k=\frac{29}{3}$
(c) At $k=7$, the area is $4$ square units
